newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: DCP, Ngai Tahu invest NZ$7.5 mln each in Ryman.
newsitem.headline: DCP, Ngai Tahu invest NZ$7.5 mln each in Ryman.

text.p: Investment company Direct Capital Partners said on Friday it was taking a 25 percent stake in Christchurch-based Ryman Healthcare, which operates retirement villages throughout New Zealand's South Island, for NZ$7.5 million.
DCP managing director Ross George said that Maori interest Ngai Tahu Holdings was also taking a 25 percent stake in the company for the same consideration.
"Ryman Healthcare is a Christchurch-based healthcare operation which is focused primarily in the retirement village market," Ross told Reuters in a telephone interview.
"We are investing with a co-investment partner, Ngai Tahu Holdings. From our point of view, Ngai Tahu have got quite similar investment criteria to us. There's quite a lot of commonality," he said.
The controlling 50 percent of Ryman would remain with owners John Ryder and Kevin Hickman. "They have been in the business since 1984 and they've been highly successful," Ross said.
Ross said Ryman operated three retirement villages in Christchurch, two in Dunedin and one in Invercargill. The complexes contained facilities such as apartments, rest homes, hospitals and studios.
Ross said DCP had been looking to invest in the health secotor for some time.
"Probably 12 months ago we looked at the health industry generally -- it's an industry area that we've got a real level of interest in," he said.
"One of the things that hits you very early on in that analysis is the ageing population distribution in this country.

"The retirement village industry in New Zealand is relatively young and we don't have the percentage of our retired people in retirement villages certainly that Australia does, or the U.S. or the U.K.
"There is a macro trend... and an industry or behavioural trend for increasing use of these facilities."
